findings.title: Existing DuckDB-backed tests for TablesList/NewSQLCommand will now fail
findings.body:
`TablesList` now calls the stub `NewInMemoryDB().RunCommands`, which always returns "not implemented". `NewSQLCommand` then always fails with `sql-invalid-sql`.

The existing unit tests in `pkg/expr/sql` (parser tests) and `pkg/expr/sql_command_test.go` call `TablesList`/`NewSQLCommand` with real SQL and assert on the returned table names. This PR does not update, skip or remove them, so they will fail and break CI.

They should be skipped or rewritten to assert the new disabled behaviour.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions are rejected on both code paths
findings.body:
This is the in-repo fix for CVE-2024-9264, but no test asserts that SQL expressions are refused.

There are two entry points:
- `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` (the new gate at line 129).
- The legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` -> `NewSQLCommand` path. It does not go through the reader gate and is protected only by the stub DB.

Without tests for both, someone could later restore a real DB implementation or change `enableSqlExpressions`, and nothing would fail to flag the reintroduced RCE/LFI. Add tests that a `type: sql` query fails in `ReadQuery`, and that `NewSQLCommand`/`Execute` cannot run SQL.

findings.title: enableSqlExpressions reads the feature flag but always returns false
findings.body:
The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions)`, so the variable named `enabled` actually means the flag is disabled. Both branches then return `false`.

The flag lookup is dead logic, and the function name, variable name and control flow all suggest the feature can be enabled by the toggle when it cannot. That misleads future maintainers and anyone debugging why enabling `sqlExpressions` has no effect.

Replace it with an explicit hard-disable plus a comment referencing the CVE, or make the intended re-enable condition explicit and correct.

findings.title: Misleading and inconsistent errors when SQL expressions are used
findings.body:
On the reader path the user gets "sqlExpressions is not implemented". That is inaccurate: the feature exists but has been deliberately disabled for security.

On the legacy `UnmarshalSQLCommand` path (used when the expression parser toggle is off), the request fails inside `TablesList`. The user gets a BadRequest "error reading SQL command", which implies their SQL is invalid. Each attempt also logs at Error level in `parser.go` (and Warn in `sql_command.go`), including the raw user SQL.

Users who enabled the `sqlExpressions` flag get confusing feedback, and logs get noisy. Return a single clear "SQL expressions are disabled" error from both paths, ideally before calling `TablesList`.
